authoredFrom: the gates table in kaambaan apps/api/src/board/board-do.ts, the GateDecision union it resolves against, and charter decisions/2026-08-30-a-gate-closes-over-chat.md
purpose: A kaambaan approval gate crosses into a Matrix room and a human's answer crosses back. Three codebases must agree on the field names: the board that opens the gate, the Application Service that projects and resolves it, and the client that draws the buttons. A rename in any one of them is a gate that silently never resolves — which reads to the human as a button that does nothing.

howToRead.wireShape: The two directions are DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC. Outbound, a gate is a genuine custom Matrix event type `dev.kaambaan.gate.v1`, matching the three `dev.agentpod.*` types already shipping, because it needs a renderer: it is a question with buttons. Inbound, a decision is an ordinary `m.room.message` with `msgtype: "m.text"` carrying `suite_event_type` in content, because it needs no renderer: it is a sentence, and sending it as a message means it reads in every client with no registry entry and no risk of a reader seeing their own answer twice.
howToRead.versioning: Major version in the `suite_event_type` string (`.v1` → `.v2`) mints a new type and a new renderer. Minor version is `schema_version`, an integer inside content, bumped for additive changes only. A renderer written against v1 tolerates a higher schema_version by ignoring fields it does not know.
howToRead.accept: Payloads a consumer MUST handle. Field names here are the contract.
howToRead.reject: Payloads a consumer MUST refuse. These are the point of the corpus — a fixture of only-valid examples proves almost nothing, which is how the mem_/mbr_ drift survived in kaambaan for as long as both halves existed.
howToRead.stockClients: A stock client renders an unknown EVENT TYPE as nothing at all — not as fallback text. So a gate is accompanied by a companion prose m.room.message carrying the same question. That is the suite's existing convention, documented on supermessage's PermissionRequestRenderer: the event is sent beside an ordinary prose message so a client that never renders it is "exactly as able to answer as it was". kaambaan#34 assumed a custom event's own `body` would be shown by every client; that is true of an unknown MSGTYPE and not of an unknown EVENT TYPE.
howToRead.whichConsumer: `reject` binds the SENDER and the Application Service: payloads that must not be emitted and must not be acted on. It does NOT ask a renderer to refuse an unrecognised field — additive tolerance is required in the other direction, and a renderer refusing unknown keys would break the moment `schema_version` is bumped. A renderer's obligation for a reject case is narrower: offer no decision it cannot honestly resolve.

optionIds.meaning: NOT free-form. kaambaan's resolveGate takes `GateDecision = 'approve' | 'request_changes' | 'reject'`, so an option id outside this set renders a button that is refused on resolution. kaambaan#34 proposed free-form ids mirroring a `select` signal's semantics; that is a good instinct and it is not what the endpoint does. Widening gates to arbitrary options is a `.v2`, not a field change.
optionIds.labelsAreFree: `label` is display text and carries no meaning. Per-board wording belongs there.

droppedDeliberately.run_id: There is no run column on a gate. A gate is card-and-stage scoped. kaambaan#34 asked whether run_id was meaningful here; it is not.
droppedDeliberately.task_id: No such row exists in kaambaan's model. The pair is card and stage.
droppedDeliberately.expires_at: Gates do not expire. No column, no sweep, no alarm. An optional field nothing will ever set invites client code for an impossible case.
droppedDeliberately.tenant_id: kaambaan's internal isolation boundary. A room may have wider membership than a board, and no consumer needs it — the Application Service recorded which board a gate came from. (#34's sketch also wrote the prefix as `tn_`; the grammar pins `tnt_`.)

events.sender: the station's own virtual user, so the question comes from the agent whose room it is

content.prompt: Ship the OAuth change to staging?

accept.why: a higher schema_version is tolerated — a v1 renderer reads the fields it knows and ignores the rest

content.body: Approval needed — "Rotate the signing key" at stage `review`.

accept.why: two options rather than three — a gate need not offer request_changes

content.body: Approval needed — "Delete the staging bucket" at stage `review`.

reject.why: an option id outside GateDecision. Renders a fine button and is refused on resolution — the failure this corpus exists to make loud.
no body. A message with nothing for a stock client to render defeats the reason the marker shape was chosen.
carries tenant_id. Dropped deliberately; its presence means a sender built against the superseded #34 sketch.
carries run_id, task_id and expires_at — all three dropped. Same superseded sketch.
empty options. A decision with nothing to choose is a card that cannot be answered; it must not render as pending.
duplicate option ids. Resolution is by id, so two `approve` entries are ambiguous regardless of their labels.

events.companion: Sent beside a plain m.room.message carrying the same question, so stock clients can follow the room. The companion is prose only and carries no structured fields; nothing resolves against it.
events.bodyIsForThisClient: `body` is supermessage's own FallbackBody path, used when the renderer cannot draw the card — not a stock-client fallback. That is what the companion message is for.

events.sender: the human's own Matrix session, so the actor is carried inherently. charter decisions/2026-08-14-approvals-cross-planes-as-events.md turns on this: a bridge substituting its own identity would void kaambaan's separation-of-duties check and every approval in the suite would attribute to one account.

notes.bothIdentifiers: `gate_id` AND the m.relates_to reference, deliberately. The reference is what a client uses to thread the answer under the question; `gate_id` is what the Application Service resolves on. Trusting only the reference would mean resolving a gate by chasing an event id an untrusted sender chose; trusting only `gate_id` would leave the answer visually unmoored. They MUST agree, and a consumer refuses when they do not.
notes.comment: Not decoration. On `request_changes`, kaambaan merges it into the card's handoff as `feedback`, so the rework carries the reviewer's reasoning. A client should prompt for text on that option and no other.

content.body: Approved — Ship the OAuth change to staging?

accept.why: request_changes, carrying the feedback that becomes the rework's context

content.body: Requested changes — Ship the OAuth change to staging?
content.comment: Add a test for the refresh-token path first.

reject.why: no m.relates_to. The answer names a gate but is bound to no question, so nothing proves the sender saw the gate they claim to answer.
a reply relation rather than a reference. m.in_reply_to is a rendering hint any client sets when quoting; treating it as a decision binding would let an ordinary quoted reply resolve a gate.
missing gate_id — the field resolution actually keys on

events.discriminator: `suite_event_type` in content, because the Matrix event type is m.room.message. The Application Service switches on it.
